prompt: A patient is upset and asks for a 100% refund. What should frontline staff do FIRST?
choices: Promise the refund to calm them down
Use empathy, follow written policy, and loop in billing — no refund promise
Waive the fee because the provider seems okay with it
Cancel and refund in Clarity without telling billing
explain: False refund/discount promises are a compliance and revenue-integrity risk. Provider sympathy does not replace billing approval.

prompt: Patient cancels an appointment scheduled for TODAY at 6 PM (within the late-cancel window). Refund?
choices: Yes — always refund if they ask nicely
No automatic refund — explain late-cancel policy and route billing questions to billing lead / Clarity support
explain: Training emphasis: same-day/inside-window cancels are typically non-refundable per Clarity policy — confirm exact window with billing lead; never promise in chat.

prompt: Provider cannot join due to emergency. Best first step?
choices: Offer reschedule without charging again; refund only if billing/provider approves
explain: Reschedule first. Refunds are not automatic unless policy + billing say so.

prompt: Patient no-show for a 10:35 PM visit. Do you lead with offering a refund?
choices: No — explain no-show policy; if they dispute, billing/Clarity path; document
explain: No-show fees/refunds follow policy; don't volunteer refunds. Escalate disputes to billing.

prompt: 24+ hours before visit, card was charged twice and failed. Slot still booked. Action?
choices: Follow ops rules: after failed capture window, cancel slot so others can book; document
explain: Free the slot per workflow when payment cannot be captured in time — exact steps in ops SOP + Clarity.

prompt: Which is a billing compliance risk?
choices: Charging wrong visit type (e.g. PCP price vs controlled follow-up price)
Sending patient the public pricing page
Tagging billing on a refund request
explain: Wrong charge amounts and unauthorized refunds both harm revenue integrity — escalate to billing.

prompt: Patient asks if you accept FSA cards.
choices: Yes we always accept — I'll add your card anywhere
We often can run FSA/HSA cards in Clarity/Carepatron when eligible, but success depends on the card/plan — billing can confirm
Take card number in Siya Assistant chat
explain: FSA/HSA depend on plan and appointment type. Cards are added only in approved payment systems — never in staff assistant chat.

prompt: HSA card declined for this visit type. Best reply?
choices: Guarantee it will work next time
Explain it may not cover this visit type; ask billing team; offer alternate payment per policy
explain: Some HSAs restrict visit types. Staff defer to billing — don't guess.

prompt: Patient paid twice; portal already shows one refund processed. You should:
choices: Confirm duplicate refund in billing portal, explain timeline politely, billing if still wrong
explain: Verify ledger before second refund. Use secure channels for account details.

prompt: Refunding in Clarity without billing lead awareness is:
choices: An workflow incident and compliance issue
explain: Billing tagged on refunds per team process — skipping billing breaks workflow and policy.
